metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Media
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Media APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that returns WordPress's image source data for an attachment.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_media_001()` delegates to `wp_get_attachment_image_src()` with the supplied attachment ID and size, returning WordPress's four-item source array for full and intermediate image sizes or `false` when no image source is available. Runtime validation uses attachment metadata instead of a real upload file and verifies URL, dimensions, and intermediate-size state.
requirements: Use WordPress media APIs
Accept the attachment ID and requested image size as inputs
Return the WordPress image source array without parsing attachment metadata manually

runtime_checks.setup: $attachment_id = wp_insert_attachment( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP Media 001', 'post_mime_type' => 'image/jpeg', 'guid' => home_url( '/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/wpbp-media-001.jpg' ) ) ); update_post_meta( $attachment_id, '_wp_attached_file', '2026/06/wpbp-media-001.jpg' ); update_post_meta( $attachment_id, '_wp_attachment_metadata', array( 'width' => 640, 'height' => 480, 'file' => '2026/06/wpbp-media-001.jpg', 'sizes' => array( 'medium' => array( 'file' => 'wpbp-media-001-300x225.jpg', 'width' => 300, 'height' => 225, 'mime-type' => 'image/jpeg' ) ) ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_media_001_attachment'] = (int) $attachment_id;

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_media_001' ) ) { return false; } $attachment_id = (int) $GLOBALS['wpbp_media_001_attachment']; $full = wpbp_media_001( $attachment_id, 'full' ); $medium = wpbp_media_001( $attachment_id, 'medium' ); return is_array( $full ) && str_ends_with( $full[0], '/2026/06/wpbp-media-001.jpg' ) && 640 === $full[1] && 480 === $full[2] && false === $full[3] && is_array( $medium ) && str_ends_with( $medium[0], '/2026/06/wpbp-media-001-300x225.jpg' ) && 300 === $medium[1] && 225 === $medium[2] && true === $medium[3] && false === wpbp_media_001( 0, 'full' );
assertions.description: The function returns WordPress attachment image source arrays for full and intermediate sizes

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_media_001( int $attachment_id, string|array $size = 'thumbnail' ): array|false { return wp_get_attachment_image_src( $attachment_id, $size ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that returns post content after WordPress applies media tag optimizations.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_media_002()` passes the supplied HTML and optional context to `wp_filter_content_tags()`. Runtime validation creates image attachment metadata, filters an image tag with a matching `wp-image-*` class, and checks that WordPress adds dimensions and responsive image attributes rather than leaving the tag unchanged.
requirements: Use WordPress media APIs
Accept the HTML string and optional context as inputs
Return the filtered HTML string

tests.prompt: Implement a function that returns WordPress image resize dimensions.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_media_003()` forwards the original size, requested size, and crop setting to `image_resize_dimensions()`. Runtime validation checks proportional downscaling, verifies WordPress refuses an upscale-only resize, and checks explicit crop positioning.
requirements: Use WordPress media APIs
Accept the original dimensions, requested dimensions, and crop setting as inputs
Return the WordPress resize dimensions array or false
tests.test_function: wpbp_media_003( int $orig_w, int $orig_h, int $dest_w, int $dest_h, bool|array $crop = false ): array|false

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_media_003' ) ) { return false; } $scaled = wpbp_media_003( 600, 300, 300, 300, false ); $upscale = wpbp_media_003( 300, 150, 600, 300, false ); $cropped = wpbp_media_003( 600, 300, 200, 200, array( 'left', 'top' ) ); return array( 0, 0, 0, 0, 300, 150, 600, 300 ) === $scaled && false === $upscale && array( 0, 0, 0, 0, 200, 200, 300, 300 ) === $cropped;
assertions.description: The function returns WordPress resize arrays for scale and crop cases and false for upscaling

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_media_003( int $orig_w, int $orig_h, int $dest_w, int $dest_h, bool|array $crop = false ): array|false { return image_resize_dimensions( $orig_w, $orig_h, $dest_w, $dest_h, $crop ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that reads embedded image alternative text from a file path.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_media_004()` loads the admin image helper if needed and calls `wp_get_image_alttext()` for the supplied file path. Runtime validation uses a temporary image-like file containing IPTC/XMP `AltTextAccessibility` metadata and a second file without XMP data, expecting the embedded alternative text for the first and an empty string for the second.
requirements: Use WordPress media APIs
Load the admin image helper before calling wp_get_image_alttext
Return an empty string when no embedded alternative text is present

tests.prompt: Implement a function that returns WordPress's extension and MIME type result for an upload filename.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_media_005()` calls `wp_check_filetype()` with the supplied filename and optional MIME map, returning the `ext` and `type` array from WordPress. Runtime validation checks a normal JPEG filename, an unknown extension, and a custom MIME map to ensure the implementation uses WordPress's extension-based file-type lookup.
requirements: Use WordPress file type APIs
Accept an optional MIME map
Do not inspect file contents

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_media_005' ) ) { return false; } $jpeg = wpbp_media_005( 'photo.jpg' ); $unknown = wpbp_media_005( 'photo.notallowed' ); $custom = wpbp_media_005( 'payload.wpbp', array( 'wpbp' => 'application/x-wpbp' ) ); return 'jpg' === $jpeg['ext'] && 'image/jpeg' === $jpeg['type'] && false === $unknown['ext'] && false === $unknown['type'] && 'wpbp' === $custom['ext'] && 'application/x-wpbp' === $custom['type'];
assertions.description: The function returns WordPress file-type results for allowed, unknown, and custom extensions

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_media_005( string $filename, ?array $mimes = null ): array { return wp_check_filetype( $filename, $mimes ); }

tests.prompt: Extend the media library so files with the .wpbp extension and the MIME type application/x-wpbp may be uploaded by users who are allowed to manage options, while everyone else keeps WordPress's default set of allowed types unchanged. WordPress asks this question about a specific user in some code paths and about whoever is logged in in others, and both must be answered correctly.
tests.expected_behavior: A callback on the allowed-upload-types filter accepts both the types array and the user WordPress is asking about, and grants the extra type only when that user can `manage_options`. Because the user argument is `null` when WordPress is asking about the current user, the callback must fall back to `current_user_can()` in that case; registering the filter with a single accepted argument, or ignoring the argument entirely, gets one of the two paths wrong. The default types are returned untouched.
requirements: Register the extra type through the WordPress filter for allowed upload types
Grant the type only to users who can manage options
Answer correctly both when WordPress names the user and when it means the current user
Leave WordPress's default types in place

required_patterns.description: Uses the allowed upload types filter
Gates on the manage options capability
Answers for the user WordPress names

'wp-admin/includes/user.php'; foreach ( array( 'wpbp_media_006_admin', 'wpbp_media_006_sub' ) as $key ) { $id = (int) ( $GLOBALS[ $key ] ?? 0 ); if ( $id > 0 ) { wp_delete_user( $id ); } unset( $GLOBALS[ $key ] ); }

tests.prompt: Configure this site so WordPress never advertises a responsive image candidate wider than 900 pixels, then implement a function that returns the srcset value WordPress generates for the supplied attachment at the supplied size. Change how WordPress builds the candidate list rather than editing the string it produces, and do not defeat any exception WordPress makes for the source it is actually rendering.
tests.expected_behavior: A filter on the maximum srcset image width returns 900, and the function delegates to `wp_get_attachment_image_srcset()`. `wp_calculate_image_srcset()` drops every candidate wider than the cap except the one matching the `src` being rendered, so requesting a size wider than the cap still advertises that size itself while the wider siblings disappear. Trimming the finished srcset string instead removes that source too.
requirements: Apply the 900 pixel cap through the WordPress filter for the maximum srcset candidate width
Return WordPress's srcset value for the supplied attachment and size
Do not post-process the srcset string WordPress produces

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_media_007( int $attachment_id, string|array $size ): string|false { $srcset = wp_get_attachment_image_srcset( $attachment_id, $size ); if ( ! is_string( $srcset ) ) { return $srcset; } $kept = array(); foreach ( explode( ',', $srcset ) as $candidate ) { $candidate = trim( $candidate ); if ( 1 === preg_match( '/ (\\d+)w$/', $candidate, $m ) && (int) $m[1] <= 900 ) { $kept[] = $candidate; } } return implode( ', ', $kept ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that returns WordPress's markup for an attachment at a requested size, applying the supplied extra attributes and letting WordPress resolve everything it knows about the attachment itself: the alternative text stored with the attachment, and the loading and decoding behaviour that follows from the attributes it is given. An attachment that has no image source must produce an empty string.
tests.expected_behavior: The function delegates to `wp_get_attachment_image( $attachment_id, $size, false, $attr )`. WordPress fills `alt` from the attachment's stored alternative text (empty string when there is none) unless the caller overrides it, omits the `loading` attribute entirely when the caller passes `false` for it, and drops a `decoding` value that is not one of `async`, `sync` or `auto` instead of printing it. Building the tag by hand loses all three behaviours.
requirements: Use WordPress's attachment image markup API rather than assembling the tag
Pass the requested size and the supplied attributes through to WordPress
Return an empty string when WordPress has no image for the attachment

required_patterns.description: Uses the attachment image markup API

tests.prompt: Implement a function that imports a batch of files that already live on this server into the media library, attaching each one to the supplied post, and returns the new attachment IDs in the order the files were given. Each entry of the batch is an array with the file's intended name under the key 'name' and the path of the file on disk under the key 'tmp_name'. Nothing arrives through an HTTP form here, so WordPress's form validation must be skipped, and the imported files must end up in the uploads directory rather than staying where they were.
tests.expected_behavior: The function loads the admin helpers it needs (`wp-admin/includes/file.php`, `media.php` and `image.php` are not loaded on the front end) and calls `media_handle_sideload()` for each entry, which itself passes `test_form => false` to the sideload handler. WordPress moves each file into the uploads directory, so the original paths no longer exist afterwards, creates one attachment per file parented to the supplied post, and generates its metadata. `wp_handle_upload()` would reject these files because they were never uploaded through PHP.
requirements: Use WordPress's sideload API to import files that are already on the server
Load the admin includes those functions live in before calling them
Attach every imported file to the supplied post
Return the attachment IDs in the order the files were supplied
